CanvasManager · guide for new users · updated October 2026

Getting Started with CanvasManager

Run a Canvas course from a folder of markdown files: set it up in ten minutes, see the semester on a calendar, and publish with one click.

What CanvasManager is

CanvasManager is a web app you run on your own machine that turns a folder of markdown files into a Canvas course. Every assignment, quiz, page and lecture is a plain text file. You edit the files (in the app or in any editor), the app shows them on a semester calendar, and one click publishes an item to Canvas with its dates, rubric, module placement and formatting.

Files are the truthCourse content is markdown in a folder you own. Put it in git and you get history, branches and diffs for free.
Calendar firstSee the whole semester at once. Drag an item to a new day and its dates move.
One-click publishCreate or update the Canvas item, its rubric and module entry. The calendar shows what is out of sync.
Reuse next semesterImport a previous semester's course and shift everything onto the new dates.

How your course lives on disk

You point the app at one storage folder. Inside it, each course is a folder with a settings.yml and one folder per module. Most people keep one folder per class and a subfolder per semester.

faculty/                                  ← the storage folder (mount this)
  globalSettings.yml                      ← which course folders to show in the UI
  4620_Distributed/
    2026-fall/
      Modules/
        settings.yml                      ← dates, class days, defaults, grading categories
        00 - lectures/
          week-01/
            1-Monday.md
            3-Wednesday.md
        01 Chaos KV/
          assignments/
            W01 Single-Node KV Store.md
          quizzes/
            W03 Reading Quiz.md
          pages/
            KV Wire Protocol Spec.md
        02 Async Messaging/
          ...

globalSettings.yml lists the course folders you want to see right now, so old semesters can stay on disk without cluttering the app:

courses:
  - path: ./4620_Distributed/2026-fall/Modules/
    name: Distributed
  - path: ./3630_Mobile/2026-fall/Modules/
    name: Mobile

The app edits this file for you when you add or import a course. You can also edit it by hand.

Setting it up

You need Docker and a Canvas API token. Everything runs in one container.

Canvas token

  1. In Canvas, open Account › Settings and scroll to Approved Integrations.
  2. Click New Access Token, give it a purpose like “CanvasManager”, and copy the token. Canvas shows it only once.
  3. Create a file named .env next to your compose file:
CANVAS_TOKEN=paste-your-token-here
# optional, only for the Classroom 50 (GitHub Classroom) buttons:
GH_TOKEN=ghp_...

The token acts as you in Canvas. Keep .env out of git.

Docker Compose

Save this as docker-compose.yml and adjust the three volume paths to your machine:

services:
  canvas_manager:
    image: snowcollege/canvas_management:4
    user: "1000:1000"
    container_name: canvas-manager
    ports:
      - 3000:3000
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      - storageDirectory=/app/storage
      - TZ=America/Denver
      - NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_FILE_SYNC=true
    volumes:
      - ./globalSettings.yml:/app/globalSettings.yml
      - ~/projects/faculty:/app/storage
      - ~/projects/facultyFiles:/app/public/images/facultyFiles
LineWhy
user: "1000:1000"Files the app writes are owned by you, not root. Use your own uid if it differs (id -u).
TZDue times are interpreted in this zone. Set it to your campus.
globalSettings.ymlCreate it first with just courses: [].
/app/storageYour course folder. Make it a git repo.
facultyFilesOptional. Images you reference from markdown; see Images and files.

First run

echo "courses: []" > globalSettings.yml
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Open http://localhost:3000. An empty course list with two buttons is what success looks like.

When a newer image is on Docker Hub the home page shows a banner with the commits it contains. Nothing updates on its own; run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d when you want it.

Adding a course

  • Add New Course creates a folder and settings.yml, and asks which Canvas course it maps to. You can also choose an existing course to import content from; assignments, quizzes, pages and lectures are copied and shifted onto the new semester's dates.
  • Import Existing Course adds a folder that already has a settings.yml (a colleague's course, or a semester you removed from the list) back into globalSettings.yml.
  • Delete Mode removes a course from the list. Files on disk are not touched.

Course settings

Open a course and click Course Settings in the top right. Set these before you start publishing.

SettingWhat it does
Days of weekWhich days the class meets. Those days are shaded on the calendar and offered by the date picker.
Semester start and endBounds the calendar and the “next class day” helper.
Classroom 50Optional GitHub Classroom integration. Skip it unless you use Classroom 50.
Default submission types and upload typesWhat new assignments start with.
Default due time and lock offsetThe time of day dragged items get, and how many hours after due an assignment locks.
Assignment groupsCanvas grading categories and their weights. Update Assignment Groups In Canvas pushes them; do that once at the start of a semester.
Students and GroupsRead-only views of the Canvas roster and group sets, used by the editor. See the Group Assignments & Student Schedules guide.
HolidaysDays with no class. They are labeled on the calendar and struck through in the date picker.

The calendar

The course page is a calendar of the whole semester with the module list beside it. Each item is a pill on its due day, and the border tells you its Canvas state:

  • Green: published and matches Canvas.
  • Red: in Canvas but different (dates, description, rubric, points, group set, assignment group, or not published). Hover to read every difference, with a link to the compare page.
  • Grey: only on disk, not in Canvas yet.

The icon at the right of each pill tells the type apart: a blue pencil for an assignment, an amber question mark for a quiz, a violet page for a page. The same icon sits before the item’s name at the top of its editor.

Things you can do from the calendar:

  • Hover a published item to preview its content; hover a red one to see everything that differs.
  • Drag an item to another day. Due, lock and unlock dates move together, keeping their spacing. Lectures can be dragged too.
  • Right-click an item for a menu: publish, view, compare, update or delete in Canvas, duplicate, rename. Publish turns into a green Published once students can see it.
  • Click the + on a day to create a new item due that day, or click the day's title to open that day's lecture.
  • Reload Canvas Data refreshes the Canvas side of the comparison; View in Canvas opens the course.

Editing content

Every editor has the same shape: the file on the left, a live preview on the right, and a footer that says how the file stands against Canvas. Changes save to disk as you type, and the preview shows parse errors at the top in red. The file is also watched, so editing it in another program updates the app immediately.

Assignments

An assignment file is a settings block, a --- line, the description in markdown, and a ## Rubric heading followed by the criteria.

UnlockAt: 
LockAt: 09/04/2026 23:59:00
DueAt: 09/04/2026 23:59:00
AssignmentGroupName: Assignments
Classroom50Slug: 
SubmissionTypes:
- online_text_entry
- online_upload
AllowedFileUploadExtensions:
- pdf
---

Next week you'll implement primary-backup replication...

## Rubric

- 10pts: Formatting
  - 10pts: proper margins, font size, spacing, and headings
  - 7pts: margins and font size correct but missing heading styles
- 5pts: Student response to reading
- 2pts: (extra credit) Went beyond the prompt
  • Dates are MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS. UnlockAt and LockAt may be blank.
  • Each rubric line is - Npts: label (pt for a single point; decimals work). Indented lines under a criterion become ratings the grader can pick from. Labels starting with (extra credit), and negative rows used as deductions, do not count toward points possible.
  • Markdown, tables, Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX math and images all render in Canvas.
  • Link to another page, assignment or quiz by its relative path, like [spec](<../pages/Wire Protocol Spec.md>). The preview opens it in the app, and publishing rewrites it to the Canvas url.
  • The ? button at the bottom left opens a searchable reference with copyable examples for every setting and syntax.

Quizzes

A quiz file has its own settings block, then one question per section separated by --- lines. The preview renders each question the way Canvas will.

  • Points: N on a question's first line sets its points; without it the question is worth 1.
  • The question text is markdown, then the answers. The last lines decide the question type:
TypeHow to write it
Multiple choicea) ..., b) ...; a * in front marks the correct one
Multiple answers[*] right and [ ] wrong checkboxes
Essaya last line of essay
Short answera last line of short_answer (graded by hand), or starred answers followed by short_answer= to auto-grade
Numerical= 2.5 for an exact answer, = [2.4, 2.6] for a range
Matching^ left - right lines; ^ - extra adds a distractor
Multiple dropdownsmatching lines split into groups by blank lines; each prompt gets its own dropdown of its group's answers
Fill in multiple blanks[ans1] placeholders in the question, then [ans1] = answer for each blank; more accepted answers for the same blank go on the next lines as = answer
  • Lines beginning + and - before the answers are feedback for correct and incorrect answers; ... is shown either way.
  • Code blocks work in questions and answers, and answer markers inside a code block are ignored.
  • The quiz help (the ? button) has a copyable example of every type.

Pages

Pages are plain markdown with one setting, DueDateForOrdering, which only decides where the page sits on the calendar and in the module.

Lectures

Each class day has one lecture file with a name, a date and markdown notes. Click a day's title on the calendar to open it. preview opens a full-width view for projecting.

Editor helpers

The settings block has autocomplete. A blank line offers the keys the file is missing; a key like AssignmentGroupName offers its valid values; a - under a list offers the list's options. Date fields open a date and time picker that knows your class days and holidays.

The help panel is searchable: type a word like rubric, numerical or schedule to filter it to the topics that mention it. Expand all and Collapse all sit beside the search box, and every example has a Copy button.

Publishing to Canvas

Each editor’s footer says where the item stands and shows the one button you need next:

  • Not in Canvas yet: Add to Canvas creates the item in Canvas, unpublished, with its rendered description, dates, rubric and module entry. A module that does not exist yet is created.
  • 3 differences from Canvas (in amber): Update in Canvas pushes the current file over the existing Canvas item. Submissions and grades are untouched. Click the amber text to open Compare with Canvas.
  • In sync · students can’t see it yet: Publish in Canvas makes it visible to students. If the item’s module is still unpublished in Canvas, the app says so and links to the modules page; it does not publish the module for you.
  • In sync · Published: nothing to do; View in Canvas opens it.
  • For a quiz, Update in Canvas also replaces the questions with the file’s. If students have already started, it asks first: their attempts keep the questions they got and are not regraded.
  • Pages are not compared field by field, so a page’s footer says Published or students can’t see it yet and keeps Update in Canvas as its button.

Everything else is behind the arrow on the right edge of that button: View in Canvas, Compare with Canvas, Update in Canvas anyway, Classroom 50, and, at the bottom in red, Delete from Canvas (removes it there and leaves your file alone) or Delete locally for an item that is only on disk. At the left are the help button, previous and next item, and Back to calendar. On a phone all of these are in the ☰ menu.

Published quiz? Click “Save it now”. After updating the questions of a published quiz, students keep getting the old questions until you open the quiz in Canvas and click Save it now. The Canvas API cannot do that step. The app reminds you with a message that links to the quiz.

The calendar border and the right-click menu do the same jobs from the course page, so a typical week is: write the files, glance at the calendar for grey and red pills, publish or update from the menu.

Publishing uses your Canvas token, so it can do anything you can. The app never deletes a Canvas item unless you ask it to.

Compare with Canvas

When an item’s border is red, Compare with Canvas (the amber differences from Canvas text in the editor footer, the menu on the footer’s main button, the right-click menu, and the red pill’s hover card) opens a page that lists every difference between your file and Canvas:

  • A settings table with the file’s value and Canvas’s side by side: published state, dates, assignment group, group set, points and each rubric row.
  • For a quiz, a row for every question, compared on type, points, text, answers (correct ones marked ✓) and feedback. A matching question shows its first line; one that differs shows only the parts that differ. The quiz editor’s footer counts these differences too. The calendar checks questions for this week’s quizzes and the next three weeks’, fetching them in the background one quiz at a time (this week first) so Canvas doesn’t throttle you; a quiz outside those four weeks gets its red border from settings and description only.
  • The description side by side, as changes only (a word-level diff), or as the normalized HTML when you need to see why two descriptions that look the same count as different.
  • An Update Canvas button at the bottom that pushes the file, with a note saying exactly what it will change.

Images and files

Mount a folder of images at /app/public/images/facultyFiles (see the compose file) and reference them from markdown:

![formulas](/images/facultyFiles/1405/lab-04-simple-math-formulas.png)

When you publish, the image is uploaded to the course's Canvas files once and the link is rewritten to the Canvas copy. The mapping is remembered in settings.yml. Public web URLs work as-is. Keep images in a separate repo from your course text so the text repo stays small.

Tips

  • Make the storage folder a git repo and commit as you go. The files are small and diff well. No student names are written to them.
  • Edit anywhere. The app watches the folder, so a change made in your own editor shows up in the app within a second.
  • Start a semester from the previous one. Add New Course, choose the old course to import from, and everything lands on the new dates ready to review.
  • Push assignment groups once, at the start of the semester, then check the “Weight final grade based on assignment groups” box in Canvas.
  • Read the red pills. Hovering an out-of-sync item tells you exactly what differs, which is faster than opening Canvas to compare.
  • Error messages stay until you close them, so you will not miss one, and the same error repeated shows once instead of stacking.
  • Group projects and per-student due dates have their own guide: Group Assignments & Student Schedules.
